# iOS layer configuration thread patch

This directory contains crates.io wgpu-hal 30.0.1 from upstream commit 40f4a34ebaf56f9a046231f54125ad046239d3f3 in wgpu-hal. The package checksum is b6b7fb58561a792bc237628ba0792e332de418fefe145f13b5ed8201e6d52f58. Registry bookkeeping and the unused package lockfile are omitted. Upstream licenses are retained. KINESYNC-PROVENANCE.json records original and patched hashes for each included upstream file.

Only Cargo.toml, src/metal/mod.rs and src/metal/surface.rs differ from upstream. The added src/metal/layer_thread.rs dispatches iOS CAMetalLayer configuration to the main queue through dispatch2 0.3.1. Other platforms execute the setter block directly with upstream behavior. The dependency is restricted to iOS. Cargo.toml.orig remains the unmodified upstream manifest for provenance. The local .gitattributes preserves original bytes, including the upstream Vulkan descriptor file's CRLF line endings, so provenance hashes survive fresh checkouts.

RustOwner retains the UIView backing CAMetalLayer and owns all Rust operations on its shared serial worker. UIKit layout and lifecycle callbacks run on main. Metal surface configuration previously called layer setters on the worker, including setOpaque, which can enter UIKit through the backing layer delegate and invalidate layout during a background Core Animation transaction commit.

All initial, resize and Outdated recovery configure calls reach the same patched HAL boundary. The HAL updates its metadata on the caller, then dispatches only layer configuration to main before returning. The render_layer mutex is acquired inside the dispatched block. It is never held while waiting for main. Main-thread callers execute inline to avoid self-deadlock. Scoped Send captures keep the surface, device and configuration alive until synchronous completion. Panics are caught inside the callback and resumed on the caller so they never unwind through libdispatch.

The main thread must never synchronously wait for RustOwner.worker or call Rust while holding a lock needed by that worker. RustOwner must never hold gate across a Rust call. Lifecycle and retirement continue to enqueue asynchronously. Main may briefly acquire gate because the worker releases it before calling Rust. The iOS callback only sets layer properties and computes their arguments. It does not acquire a drawable, submit commands, poll a device or wait for GPU work. wgpu-core's wait before HAL configuration stays on the worker. Per-frame acquisition, rendering, presentation and destruction remain there too.

Debug assertions check main-thread layer configuration and worker execution of creation, resize, acquisition and Outdated recovery. Regression tests check every configure entry point, setter confinement, the dispatch boundary, dependency resolution and upstream file hashes. Linux tests cannot execute UIKit or libdispatch. An iOS Rust target check catches Metal type errors but does not compile Swift or link an application.

Before release, build the custom development IPA in macOS CI and exercise mount, rotation, rapid resize, repeated background and foreground transitions, lock and unlock, navigation teardown and rapid remount on device with Main Thread Checker enabled. Check smooth frames and responsive lifecycle callbacks while GPU work is outstanding. Outdated recovery also needs device observation or fault injection because normal resume may not produce that status. No C ABI contract changes are made. Remove the vendor patch when a pinned upstream release provides equivalent layer-thread confinement.
